name: /give
summary: Gives one or more items to a player.
description: The /give command adds items directly to a player's inventory, without needing to craft or find them. In Java Edition you can also attach NBT data to customize the item; Bedrock Edition uses a data value and the components json format instead.

examples.note: Give the nearest player a stack of 64 diamonds
Give yourself an iron sword
Give the player Steve 3 enchanted golden apples

targets: @p nearest player, @a all players, @r random player, @s yourself, @e entities (not for /give)
tips: Item names need the minecraft: namespace in Java Edition; in Bedrock it is optional.
Count is optional and defaults to 1. Maximum stack sizes still apply per item.
In Java 1.20.5+, NBT in /give was replaced by item components, e.g. /give @s diamond_sword[minecraft:custom_name='{"text":"Excalibur"}'].

name: /tp
summary: Teleports a player or entity to coordinates or to another entity.
description: /tp (alias of /teleport) instantly moves players or entities to exact coordinates, or to another entity's position. Coordinates can be absolute, relative (~) or, in Java Edition, local (^) based on where the target faces.

examples.note: Teleport yourself to x=100, y=64, z=-250
Teleport the nearest player to Steve
Teleport yourself 50 blocks straight up

targets: @s, @p, @a, @r, @e or a player name; coordinates x y z
tips: Use ~ before a number for relative movement from the current position.
Teleporting to unloaded chunks loads them; very high y values can cause fall damage on arrival.
In Java Edition /teleport and /tp are the same command.

name: /summon
summary: Spawns any mob or entity at a chosen position.
description: /summon creates an entity - a mob, item, projectile or vehicle - at the given coordinates, or at your position if none are given. Java Edition accepts NBT data for custom names, equipment, AI changes and more.

examples.note: Summon a creeper at your position
Summon a zombie villager at x=100, y=65, z=100
Strike lightning where you stand

targets: Any entity type, e.g. minecraft:zombie, minecraft:warden, minecraft:item
tips: Entity IDs use the minecraft: namespace in Java Edition.
Summoning bosses like the Wither or Ender Dragon with /summon spawns them without the usual ritual, but the fight is the same.
In Java, add NBT for custom mobs, e.g. /summon zombie ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:'{"text":"Bob"}',NoAI:1b}.

name: /locate
summary: Finds the coordinates of the nearest structure, biome or point of interest.
description: /locate searches for the closest matching structure (village, stronghold, ancient city...), biome, or point of interest and returns its coordinates, which you can click to teleport. Search radius is large, so it works even for rare structures.

examples.note: Find the nearest stronghold
Find the nearest ancient city
Find the nearest cherry grove biome (Java only)

tips: Bedrock Edition only supports /locate structure (plus /locate biome since 1.19.10 in some versions; structure is the reliable one).
Click the green coordinates in chat to get a ready /tp command.
Some structures only generate in specific dimensions, so run it in the right one (e.g. bastion_remnant in the Nether).
keywords: locate find structure biome village stronghold ancient city

name: /gamemode
summary: Switches a player between survival, creative, adventure and spectator mode.
description: /gamemode changes how a player interacts with the world: survival (health and hunger), creative (unlimited blocks, flight), adventure (no block breaking without the right tools) and spectator (fly through blocks, Java only).

examples.note: Switch yourself to creative mode
Put every player back into survival
Enter spectator mode (Java Edition only)

targets: survival, creative, adventure, spectator (Java only); optional player target
tips: Short forms work in Java: /gamemode c, /gamemode s, /gamemode a, /gamemode sp.
Spectator mode does not exist in Bedrock Edition.
On servers, changing another player's gamemode requires higher operator permissions.
keywords: gamemode creative survival adventure spectator mode

name: /fill
syntaxBedrock: /fill <from: x y z> <to: x y z> <tileName: Block> [fillMode: FillMode]
summary: Fills a region of the world with a block, or replaces blocks in it.
description: /fill places blocks in a rectangular volume between two corner coordinates. Modes control what happens to existing blocks: replace (default), destroy, hollow, keep, outline - and the replace filter lets you swap one block for another. Java Edition limits a single fill to 32,768 blocks by default.

examples.note: Fill an 11x11 platform with stone
Clear a space around you
Build a hollow glass box (Bedrock syntax)

targets: Two corners (x y z) and a block ID
tips: The default block limit (Java: commandModificationBlockLimit) is 32,768 - split big jobs into several fills.
hollow fills only the outer shell; keep only fills air blocks; outline fills only the edges.
To replace one block with another in Java: /fill x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 stone replace dirt.
keywords: fill blocks region build replace hollow

name: /effect
summary: Applies or removes status effects like speed, strength or regeneration.
description: /effect give applies a potion-style status effect to players or mobs, with a duration in seconds and an amplifier (level minus one). /effect clear removes effects. Infinite duration is supported in modern Java with the keyword infinite.

examples.note: Give yourself Speed II for 60 seconds
Permanent regeneration on the nearest player (Java)
Cure everyone of poison

targets: give or clear, an entity target, an effect ID
tips: Amplifier is level minus 1: amplifier 0 = level I, amplifier 3 = level IV.
Bedrock caps duration at high but finite values; Java 1.19.4+ accepts infinite.
Use /effect clear @s with no effect to remove everything from yourself.
keywords: effect potion status buff speed strength regeneration

name: /time
summary: Changes or queries the world's time of day.
description: /time set moves the in-game clock to a named moment (day, noon, night, midnight) or an exact tick count. /time add advances the clock, and /time query reads it. One Minecraft day lasts 24,000 ticks - 20 real minutes.

examples.note: Jump to morning (tick 1000)
Jump to night (tick 13000)
Advance the clock by 6000 ticks (5 real minutes)

tips: day = 1000, noon = 6000, sunset ~ 12000, night = 13000, midnight = 18000 ticks.
/time query day tells you how many full in-game days have passed in the world.
Freeze the daylight cycle with /gamerule doDaylightCycle false.
keywords: time day night set clock ticks

name: /weather
description: /weather sets the current weather to clear, rain or thunder, optionally for a specific duration in seconds. Without a duration the weather lasts for its normal random length.

examples.note: Stop the rain now
Ten minutes of thunderstorm - enough for a charged-creeper or Channeling session
Rain: riptide time

tips: Thunderstorms let you charge creepers, convert villagers to witches and pigs to zombified piglins with a Channeling trident.
Sleeping through a thunderstorm still works - no need to clear it for a bed.
keywords: weather command clear rain thunder storm

name: /enchant
summary: Enchants the item a player is holding.
description: /enchant applies an enchantment to the item in the target player's main hand, respecting normal compatibility rules - you cannot add Silk Touch to a Fortune pick or Sharpness to a bow. It works beyond normal levels in Java only if the enchantment allows it.

examples.note: Add Sharpness V to the sword in your hand
Unbreaking III on the held item
Mending on Steve's held item (level defaults to 1)

tips: The item must be in the main hand - offhand items are ignored.
Fails silently when the enchantment is incompatible or the level is out of range; /give with NBT/components bypasses those rules in Java.
keywords: enchant command sharpness mending held item

name: /setblock
syntaxBedrock: /setblock <position: x y z> <tileName: Block> [blockStates: block states] [oldBlockHandling: SetBlockType]
summary: Places a single block at exact coordinates.
description: /setblock changes one block at the given position to any block you name. Modes: replace (default, swaps any block), keep (only fills air), destroy (breaks the old block and drops it).

examples.note: Place a diamond block at those coordinates
Put a glass block directly under your feet
Chest pre-filled with diamonds (Java NBT)

tips: Use ~ ~ ~ for your own position, ~ ~-1 ~ for the block under you.
Chain it in command blocks with /fill for scripted builds; /fill is faster for volumes.

name: /kill
description: /kill removes the target entity immediately - mobs, items, vehicles or players (even in creative mode, players die). With no target it kills the command's executor.

examples.note: Kill every loaded zombie
Clear all dropped items on the ground - lag cleanup
Kill yourself (respawn at your spawn point)

targets: any entity; without a target, the executor
tips: @e without a type selector kills everything loaded, including armor stands, paintings and you - always add a type.
Item cleanup on servers: /kill @e[type=item] is the standard anti-lag command.
keywords: kill command remove entities clear items lag

name: /clear
description: /clear deletes matching items from a player's inventory. With no item specified it wipes the whole inventory; with an item and maxCount it removes only that many.

examples.note: Empty your entire inventory
Take up to 64 dirt from the nearest player
Remove every netherite sword Steve holds

tips: Great for adventure maps: test whether a player has an item by running /clear with maxCount 0 - it succeeds without deleting anything (Java).
Bedrock data values let you target specific potion or tool variants.

name: /spawnpoint
description: /spawnpoint changes a player's individual respawn location without needing a bed. Unlike /setworldspawn it only affects the targets you name, and it works in any dimension - set a respawn in the Nether without a respawn anchor.

examples.note: Respawn where you stand
Send every player's respawn to those coordinates
Move only Steve's respawn point

tips: Beds and respawn anchors override /spawnpoint when valid; break them and the spawnpoint applies.
For a global default for new players, use /setworldspawn instead.
keywords: spawnpoint command respawn set spawn bed nether

name: /xp
summary: Gives, sets or checks experience points and levels.
description: /xp adds or sets experience. Java uses /xp add @s 100 points or 10 levels, /xp set @s 30 levels, /xp query @s levels. Bedrock uses /xp 100 @s for points and /xp 10L @s for levels.

examples.note: Jump straight to +30 levels (Java)
100 levels in Bedrock
Reset everyone's level (Java)

tips: Negative amounts work in Java: /xp add @s -10 levels removes levels.
Levels and points are different things - adding levels costs the real curve price, so 30 levels gives far more total XP than 30 points. Our XP calculator shows the exact math.
keywords: xp command experience levels add set query
